newsitem.title: DENMARK: Downgraded banks drag Danish share index down.
newsitem.headline: Downgraded banks drag Danish share index down.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Wednesday, dragged down by solid declines in leading banks with dealers fearing further falls if Wall Street did not finish in a more positive vein.
"First the weaker dollar, then a downgrading by British investment bank HSBC James Capel of top Den Danske and Unibank unleashed across the board falls," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed 1.65 point down at 127.23 in overall bourse turnover of 883 million crowns. The KFX December future fell 1.50 point to 127.80 with 210 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Den Danske Bank shed eight crowns to end at 424, with rival Unibank losing seven crowns to close at 273 after being downgraded to sell from buy by Capel.
A.P. Moeller, hit by the weaker dollar, saw its D/S Svendborg fall 4,130 crowns to 210,500 and D/S 1912 slip 1,000 crowns to 147,000.
Otherwise Tele Danmark fell 8.35 crowns to 296.65 and GN Store Nord ended unchanged at 590 despite forecasting first ever 1997 profits for its partially-owned Sonofon mobile phone unit.
Only three KFX shares closed ahead, Topdanmark, Radiometer and ISS. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
